topics.label: Introduction and course overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the cancer biology lecture series and outlines the core learning outcomes for the session.

topics.label: Biological definition and experimental models of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer as a disruption of cellular differentiation and tissue architecture driven by accumulated genetic and epigenetic changes, alongside the experimental models used to study these processes.

topics.label: Tumour invasion, metastasis, and malignant progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish benign from malignant tumours by detailing the mechanisms, histological characteristics, and stepwise progression of local invasion and metastatic spread.

topics.label: Principles and exceptions of tumour nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the standard conventions and notable exceptions used to name and classify benign and malignant tumours by their tissue of origin.

topics.label: Mechanisms of tumour-induced morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the direct mechanical, metabolic, and organ-level processes by which primary and metastatic tumours cause clinical disease and death.

topics.label: Comparative tumour incidence across humans and other species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the incidence and prevalence of different tumour types in human populations and across diverse multicellular animals.

topics.label: Clinical presentation and screening strategies for cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how tumours present clinically and assess the methods, histological principles, and effectiveness of screening programs for various cancer types.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and summary
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by revisiting the learning outcomes and providing logistical instructions for upcoming practicals and sessions.
